mechanism_narrative: A continued recovery in transit access translates into more discretionary stops near stations and commuting corridors, lifting RETAIL_REC within four weeks. If TRANSIT keeps rising from its current depressed level while workplaces do not collapse further, retail visits should improve relative to the last month.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rises for 2 consecutive weeks from a sub-25% baseline gap
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT improved from -25.7 to -20.9 while RETAIL_REC improved from -17.1 to -13.1 at t-0w
failure_condition: If TRANSIT rises for two more weeks but RETAIL_REC does not exceed the prior 4-week mean, the mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When residential time stays elevated, people consolidate trips and delay nonessential shopping, pushing RETAIL_REC lower over the next two weeks. A persistent high RESIDENTIAL reading implies home-centered routines that suppress retail footfall.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL stayed above 10% in all four weeks
failure_condition: If RESIDENTIAL remains above 10% but RETAIL_REC rises above its last 4-week mean within 14 days, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: A joint pickup in workplaces and transit indicates fuller weekday circulation that spills into nearby shopping and dining, raising RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks. The effect is strongest when both series move upward together rather than independently.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES fell sharply at t-0w while TRANSIT continued improving
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both improve for two consecutive weeks and RETAIL_REC still falls relative to the last month, the interaction is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in park mobility relative to the prior week signals tighter outdoor activity conditions that spill over into discretionary retail, reducing RETAIL_REC within one week. The mechanism activates when PARKS falls from an already negative level and the decline is not offset by grocery trips.
candidate_trigger: PARKS declines by more than 3 points week-on-week from a negative baseline
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS moved from -15.1 to -21.9 before recovering to -16.0
failure_condition: If PARKS drops more than 3 points week-on-week but RETAIL_REC does not fall within 7 days, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained recovery in grocery and pharmacy mobility reflects normalized errand circulation, which precedes broader retail recovery after two to four weeks. When essential-trip mobility turns positive or near zero, discretionary retail should follow upward.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM moved from -3.7 to 0.4 by t-0w
failure_condition: If GROCERY_PHARM stays at or above 0 for two weeks and RETAIL_REC remains below its last 4-week mean, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: When transit stays deeply depressed while residential remains elevated, households substitute away from discretionary outings, causing retail mobility to weaken over four weeks. This homebound substitution is stronger if transit does not recover from a level near -20% and residential stays above +10%.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT remained between -25.7 and -20.9 while RESIDENTIAL stayed above 10%
failure_condition: If TRANSIT remains below -20% and RESIDENTIAL above 10% for another month but RETAIL_REC rises above the prior 4-week average, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A broad warming of outdoor leisure mobility, captured by improving parks visits, boosts shopping-linked foot traffic over the next four weeks. The effect requires PARKS to rise for at least two weeks in a row from its current depressed range.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises for 2 consecutive weeks from below -15
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS improved from -21.9 to -16.0 at t-0w after prior weakening
failure_condition: If PARKS rises for two consecutive weeks but RETAIL_REC does not improve versus the last four weeks, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: A rebound in retail mobility occurs only after transit and workplaces both stop deteriorating and residential pressure eases. In this regime, retail is delayed by commuting normalization, so the next four weeks should remain weak unless the labor-and-transit drag reverses.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES falls below -10 or TRANSIT slips back below -22
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES dropped to -12.7 at t-0w while TRANSIT stayed below -20
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES recovers above -8 and TRANSIT stays above -20 for two weeks yet RETAIL_REC still declines, the mechanism is rejected.
